questions.q: What does the lesson identify as the most common failure mode in governance communication?
options: Treating communication as a single announcement sent once, instead of a repeated set of touches over time
Communicating too frequently with stakeholders
Using too many different channels at once
Only communicating with executives
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly names the single-announcement approach as the most common failure, since people forget it by the time it matters.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the five elements the lesson says a real communication plan needs?
options: A fixed budget approved by finance
Multiple touches over time
A message tailored to each audience
A two-way path for questions
questions.explain: The lesson lists multiple touches, tailored messaging, multiple channels, a two-way path, and a visible owner — not a finance-approved budget.

questions.q: According to the lesson's tailoring table, what should a message to the 'low influence, high impact' group emphasize?
options: Exactly what changes in their daily workflow, with concrete before/after examples
The company's overall business case and financial risk
Nothing — this group needs no communication at all
A request for a public endorsement
questions.explain: The lesson's table specifically assigns practical workflow detail to the low-influence, high-impact quadrant, not business-case framing.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what does silence on a communication plan's two-way channel usually indicate?
options: Confusion or disengagement, not understanding
Complete success and full understanding
That the channel should be removed
That the plan is already finished
questions.explain: The lesson warns that silence is more often a sign of confusion or disengagement than of people fully understanding the change.

questions.q: What does the lesson say it means if the same basic questions keep coming up weeks after the 'launch' communication touch?
options: The message didn't land the first time and needs repeating, not that people are being slow
The governance program has definitely failed
The questions should be ignored going forward
The stakeholder map needs to be discarded entirely
questions.explain: The lesson frames recurring basic questions as a signal the message needs repeating, not evidence that the audience is slow or at fault.
